items.output: {"root_cause": "analytics-batch moved from nightly to hourly and runs a 24-hour aggregation scan against postgres-replica-a. That long-running query, now 2900 seconds old, blocks WAL apply on the replica through buffer pin conflicts, driving replication lag from 0.4s to 214s. profile-service writes to the primary and reads from the replica, so a user's own saved change is not yet visible on read and appears to revert. Every service metric stays green because nothing is erroring.", "category": "data-layer", "action_id": "kill_long_running_query"}

{"root_cause": "carrier-gateway's upstream carrier API had a real 12-minute outage roughly three hours ago, which correctly tripped shipping-service's circuit breaker. The breaker is configured with CB_HALF_OPEN_AFTER_S=0 and reset only on restart, so it never sends a trial request and has stayed open ever since. carrier-gateway recovered 168 minutes ago and has been idle at 3% CPU with zero inbound requests. The original fault is long gone; the breaker is now the outage.", "category": "cascading-failure", "action_id": "restart_pods"}

{"root_cause": "reconciliation-job v1.3.0 sizes its worker pool from the host CPU count and landed on a 64-vCPU node, producing 256 workers each holding its own connection. That took postgres-primary from a steady 138 connections to its 400 limit, so every other service is refused new connections. Postgres itself is healthy -- 44% CPU and 3.4ms mean query duration; the resource that ran out is the connection budget, not database capacity.", "category": "resource-exhaustion", "action_id": "rollback_deploy"}

{"root_cause": "The ingress config change standardised the target group health check path to /healthz, but public-api serves its health endpoint at /health and returns 404 for /healthz. All 14 targets failed the check within two intervals and the load balancer drained every one, returning 503 externally. The pods are healthy: their readiness probe still uses /health at 100% success and internal requests succeed at 99.9%.", "category": "config-error", "action_id": "revert_config_change"}

{"root_cause": "email-worker is deployed with the mutable tag latest and imagePullPolicy Always. A node pool scale-down rescheduled 7 of 12 pods 46 minutes ago, and those pods pulled sha256:9d1c, an unreleased build pushed at 16:02 that passes a locale_tag field the production template does not accept. The Deployment now runs two digests at once, and the 45% failure rate tracks the 7-of-12 split. No deploy was recorded because none was performed.", "category": "bad-release", "action_id": "rollback_deploy"}

{"root_cause": "fulfilment-worker v8.3.0 raised max_poll_interval_ms to 900000 but left SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS at 10000 while setting HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS to 12000 -- a heartbeat interval longer than the session timeout. Members are therefore expired by the broker before they can heartbeat, each expiry triggers another rebalance, and the group has churned through 299 rebalances without ever reaching a stable assignment. partitions_assigned is 0, so nothing is consumed and lag has grown to 220000. Kafka itself is healthy with zero under-replicated partitions and normal produce rate.", "category": "dependency-failure", "action_id": "rollback_deploy"}

{"root_cause": "report-builder's memory limit was raised from 2Gi to 24Gi 70 minutes ago to stop OOMKills, but its request was left at 2Gi. The scheduler still accounts for only 2Gi, while the pod now actually uses 22.4GiB on a node with 30Gi allocatable. The node crossed its eviction threshold at 29.4Gi used, and the kubelet evicted lower-priority and Guaranteed neighbours -- 4 ledger-service pods and 2 notification-service pods -- rather than the pod responsible. ledger-service is the victim; its own memory use is flat at 735MiB.", "category": "capacity", "action_id": "rollback_deploy"}
